title: Local structure and Noetherianity of quasi-compact flat monomorphisms
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a quasi-compact flat morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism] whose diagonal $Y\to Y\times_XY$ is an isomorphism (a monomorphism). Then $f$ is injective on points, and for every $y\in Y$ the induced local ring map $\mathcal O_{X,f(y)}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is an isomorphism. For every $x\in X$ the scheme-theoretic fibre $Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ is either empty or canonically $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$, and is nonempty exactly when $x\in f(Y)$. Here $\kappa(x)=\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x$ is the residue field. In particular $f$ is regular, meaning flat with geometrically regular fibres: after any field extension each nonempty fibre is the spectrum of that field. If $X$ is Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], then $Y$ is Noetherian; Noetherian means having a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. If $X$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], then $Y$ is reduced. These conclusions apply to $f_T:Y\times_XT\to T$ for every scheme $T\to X$, with the Noetherian and reduced conclusions conditional on $T$ being Noetherian and reduced, respectively.

source.place: VIII 2.1.12 (local-ring isomorphisms and injectivity, citing Raynaud 1968 Props. 1.1--1.2), 2.1.14 (extension of ideal centers), and 2.2.12 (regularity), printed pp.88--91. Auxiliary algebra: Stacks Tag 04VU, algebra.tex, lemma-faithfully-flat-epimorphism. The Noetherian consequence follows from extension-contraction for ideals of affine flat monomorphisms; no single Stacks tag states this combined geometric formulation.

proof.text: We prove the assertions uniformly after arbitrary base change. Fix $T\to X$, put $Z=Y\times_XT$, and write $h:Z\to T$. The diagonal hypothesis implies that $f$ is monic: if $fa=fb$, the pair $(a,b)$ factors uniquely through the diagonal, forcing $a=b$. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] then makes $h$ monic: two arrows to $Z$ with equal $T$-components have equal $Y$-components by monicity of $f$, and hence are equal. Conversely the same universal property shows that a monic arrow has invertible diagonal (the two projections of its kernel pair agree and are inverse to the diagonal). Thus $h$ satisfies the same diagonal hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], $h$ is flat and quasi-compact. The identity base change recovers $f$.

For $t\in T$, the fibre arrow $Z_t\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is monic by the preceding pullback argument. Apply [lem-sfb-monomorphism-into-field-coproduct] with a singleton index set. The subset supplied by that statement is either empty or the singleton, so the fibre is empty or its structural arrow is an isomorphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$. This isomorphism is canonical: it is the structural arrow itself. By the homeomorphism onto $h^{-1}(t)$ in [def-pc-scheme-fibre], the fibre is nonempty exactly when $t\in h(Z)$, and each such inverse-image set has exactly one point. Consequently $h$ is injective on points. After any field extension $L/\kappa(t)$, the empty fibre remains empty and the nonempty fibre becomes $\operatorname{Spec}L$, by the fibre-product universal property. A field has maximal ideal zero and Krull dimension zero, hence is a regular local ring. Thus these fibres are geometrically regular, and the already flat $h$ is regular in the stated sense.

source.place: Tag 03DP (lemma-mono-towards-spec-field), singleton case; Tag 01K1 (lemma-fibre-topological); ILO VIII 2.1.12 and 2.2.12, printed pp.88,91.

proof.text: Choose affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset Z$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset T$ with $h(V)\subset U$. Such pairs exist around every $z\in Z$: first take affine $U$ around $h(z)$, then affine $V\subset h^{-1}(U)$ around $z$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The induced map $g:V\to U$ exists by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. It is monic: $ga=gb$ gives $h j_Va=h j_Vb$, then $j_Va=j_Vb$ by monicity of $h$, then $a=b$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism]. Write $g=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ using [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The ring map $\varphi:A\to B$ is epic: for any commutative ring $C$ and $u,v:B\to C$ equal on $A$, monicity of $g$ gives $\operatorname{Spec}u=\operatorname{Spec}v$, and uniqueness in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives $u=v$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], applied to the flat arrow $h$ and these affine opens, says that $B$ is a flat $A$-module.

Fix $z\in V$, corresponding to $\mathfrak q\subset B$, and put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization], the local ring map of $h$ is $\varphi_z:A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$, $a/s\mapsto\varphi(a)/\varphi(s)$. It is epic: if two maps $B_{\mathfrak q}\to C$ agree on $A_{\mathfrak p}$, their restrictions to $B$ agree on $A$, hence agree on $B$ by Step 3; they then agree on every fraction $b/u$ because its image is the image of $b$ times the inverse of the image of $u$. The fraction description is [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. By flatness of $h$ and [def-weil-flat-morphism], this stalk map is flat and local. Therefore [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective] makes it faithfully flat, and [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-ring-epimorphism-isomorphism] makes it an isomorphism. These are precisely the induced local ring maps, not merely unspecified isomorphisms between the two rings.

source.place: Tag 00HR (lemma-local-flat-ff) and Tag 04VU (lemma-faithfully-flat-epimorphism); ILO VIII 2.1.12, printed p.88; schemes.tex Tags 01HV, 01I1 for stalk maps.

proof.text: Retain an arbitrary affine pair from Step 3 and let $J\subset B$ be any ideal. The two ring maps $B\to B\otimes_AB$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ and $b\mapsto1\otimes b$, exist by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] and agree on $A$. Since $A\to B$ is epic, they are equal. Multiplying by $1\otimes c$ gives $b\otimes c=1\otimes bc$. Apply the tensor map induced by $B\to B/J$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] to obtain $b\otimes\bar c=1\otimes\overline{bc}$. It follows directly that $\theta:B\otimes_A(B/J)\to B/J$, $b\otimes\bar c\mapsto\overline{bc}$, has inverse $\bar c\mapsto1\otimes\bar c$: the two composites are the identity on $B/J$ and on every generating pure tensor. The maps are well-defined by bilinearity and the displayed relation.

source.place: Tag 04VN (lemma-epimorphism), equality of the two tensor inclusions; Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product). The displayed quotient-module computation expands the argument directly.

proof.text: Put $I=\varphi^{-1}(J)$. The sequence $I\hookrightarrow A\to B/J$ is exact at $A$, by the definition of $I$. Tensor it with the flat $A$-module $B$ using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Identify $B\otimes_AA$ with $B$ by $b\otimes a\mapsto b\varphi(a)$ and inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$; these formulas are inverse by the balancing relation of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Under this identification and $\theta$ from Step 5, the tensored map to $B\otimes_A(B/J)$ is exactly the quotient $B\to B/J$. The image of $B\otimes_AI\to B$ is the set of finite sums $\sum b_k\varphi(i_k)$ with $i_k\in I$, namely the extended ideal $IB$. Exactness therefore gives $IB=J$. No surjectivity of $A\to B/J$ was assumed or used.

source.place: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), preservation of exactness, applied to the kernel of A -> B/J; Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product). This is the affine ideal-extension argument underlying ILO VIII 2.1.14.

proof.text: Suppose now that $T$ is Noetherian. Choose a finite affine cover $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ with every $A_i$ Noetherian, as in the statement. Since $h$ is quasi-compact, each $h^{-1}(U_i)$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The affine basis [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] supplies a finite cover of each such inverse image by affine opens $V_{ij}=\operatorname{Spec}B_{ij}$ contained in it. For any ideal $J\subset B_{ij}$, its contraction $I\subset A_i$ has finitely many generators $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Step 6 gives $J=IB_{ij}$, so $\varphi(a_1),\ldots,\varphi(a_r)$ generate $J$. Hence $B_{ij}$ is Noetherian by that same definition. The finite family $V_{ij}$ covers $Z$, proving that $Z$ is Noetherian in exactly the finite-affine-cover sense of the statement. This includes empty inverse images and the empty scheme.

source.place: VIII 2.1.14, printed pp.88--89, affine ideal-extension consequence; Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00FM (section-Noetherian), every ideal finitely generated. Agent-written consequence of Steps 3,5,6.

proof.text: If $T$ is reduced, every $\mathcal O_{T,h(z)}$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The actual stalk-map isomorphism of Step 4 then makes $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ reduced: an element whose positive power is zero pulls back under the inverse isomorphism to a nilpotent element, which is zero. Again by [def-pc-reduced-scheme], $Z$ is reduced. Since $T\to X$ was arbitrary in Step 1, all the conclusions hold for every $f_T$, with the Noetherian and reduced conclusions under exactly the corresponding assumptions on $T$. Taking $T=X$ and its identity gives the assertions for $f$ itself.

lean.statement: theorem flat_monomorphism_local_structure {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [QuasiCompact f] [Flat f] (_hdiag : IsIso (pullback.diagonal f)) : Function.Injective f ∧ (∀ y : Y, IsIso (f.stalkMap y)) ∧ (∀ x : X, (IsEmpty (f.fiber x) ∨ IsIso (f.fiberToSpecResidueField x)) ∧ (Nonempty (f.fiber x) ↔ x ∈ Set.range f)) ∧ (∀ (x : X) (K : Type u) [Field K] (ι : X.residueField x →+* K), IsEmpty (pullback (f.fiberToSpecResidueField x) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ι)) : Scheme.{u}) ∨ IsIso (pullback.snd (f.fiberToSpecResidueField x) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ι)))) ∧ (IsNoetherian X → IsNoetherian Y) ∧ (IsReduced X → IsReduced Y) ∧ (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ X), Flat (pullback.snd f g) ∧ Function.Injective (pullback.snd f g) ∧ (∀ z : (pullback f g : Scheme.{u}), IsIso ((pullback.snd f g).stalkMap z)) ∧ (∀ t : T, (IsEmpty ((pullback.snd f g).fiber t) ∨ IsIso ((pullback.snd f g).fiberToSpecResidueField t)) ∧ (Nonempty ((pullback.snd f g).fiber t) ↔ t ∈ Set.range (pullback.snd f g))) ∧ (∀ (t : T) (K : Type u) [Field K] (ι : T.residueField t →+* K), IsEmpty (pullback ((pullback.snd f g).fiberToSpecResidueField t) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ι)) : Scheme.{u}) ∨ IsIso (pullback.snd ((pullback.snd f g).fiberToSpecResidueField t) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ι)))) ∧ (IsNoetherian T → IsNoetherian (pullback f g)) ∧ (IsReduced T → IsReduced (pullback f g)))
